findings.summary: The page never renders a loading skeleton or spinner; while query.isLoading is true the feed area is simply empty, unlike the app's LoadingScreen pattern.
findings.fix: Add a loading branch before the results section, e.g. render a skeleton/spinner (or reuse LoadingScreen semantics with aria-busy) when query.isLoading, so the initial fetch shows feedback instead of a blank grid.

findings.summary: The publish modal's active mode tabs use hardcoded bg-white text-brand, which stays white in dark theme instead of using surface tokens.
findings.fix: Replace bg-white with bg-[var(--surface-raised)] (or bg-[var(--surface)]) so the active tab respects the dark theme like other raised surfaces.

findings.summary: The save-error message uses hardcoded text-red-600 instead of the danger design token.
findings.fix: Replace text-red-600 with text-[var(--danger)] to align with the design-system danger color and dark-theme support.

findings.summary: The header action and modal submit buttons reimplement button styles inline (bg-brand px-4 py-2.5 / rounded-xl bg-brand px-5 py-3) instead of reusing the shared .btn-primary class.
findings.fix: Use className="btn-primary" (with the icon child) for the header 'عنصر رسمي جديد' button and the modal submit button to match the app-wide button styling.

findings.summary: The modal close (X) button is icon-only with no accessible label.
findings.fix: Add aria-label="إغلاق" to the close button so screen readers announce its purpose.

findings.summary: The modal is a custom overlay without dialog semantics (no role="dialog", aria-modal, or labelled title) and no Escape/backdrop-close handling.
findings.fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" and aria-labelledby pointing to the modal title heading, matching the app's modal accessibility pattern.

findings.summary: The decision action button reimplements a bespoke style (bg-[var(--surface-muted)] text-brand) rather than using the shared .btn-secondary primitive.
findings.fix: Replace the inline classes with className="btn-secondary" (keeping the disabled/icon children) for consistency with secondary actions elsewhere.

findings.summary: The acknowledgement progress bar is purely visual with no accessible role or value exposed to assistive tech.
findings.fix: Add role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax (or aria-label with the count) on the progress container so the acknowledgement ratio is announced.
